title: Quentin and the Confession
premise: Dominic Sandoval, the concierge of the Hotel Verity who has quietly catalogued five years of the town's secrets, is hired by a nervous stranger named Quentin Ashe to prove that a murder scheduled for Friday hasn't happened yet. As Dominic decodes a ledger hidden in the hotel's guest registry, they discover Quentin is not preventing a murder but confessing to one he believes he will commit — a killing foretold by his own family's pattern of violence. The true target is Dominic's closest friend, and the ledger's final entry names Dominic as the witness who must choose between duty and love. In the end, Dominic rewrites the ledger's last line, saving both their friend and Quentin from his inheritance.
about_author: Marguerite Sterling is the pen name of a former night-desk clerk at a grand seaside hotel, where she collected decades of overheard confessions and unsent letters. She writes mysteries about people who see everything and say nothing until it's too late.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A pale, precise stranger named Quentin Ashe books Room 9 for one week, paying in cash with instructions: prove that on Friday, no one dies in this hotel. Dominic, amused and unsettled, accepts. The emotional beat is professional curiosity curdling into unease as Quentin's fear proves genuine.

chapters.title: Everything Filed Under V
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Searching their mental archive of the town's secrets, Dominic finds three prior deaths, each five years apart, each tied to guests of Room 9. The beat is dread: the pattern isn't coincidence, it's an appointment.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin reveals the family ledger disguised as the hotel's antique guest registry — initials, dates, and room numbers encoding every Sandoval-family crime, including one dated Friday. His confession: he believes he is fated to kill. The beat is raw, terrified honesty.

chapters.title: Room 9 Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Dominic and Quentin tear apart Room 9 and find the previous 'murders' were staged cover-ups by the hotel's old owner. Someone has been maintaining the fiction — and recently. The beat shifts from fatalism to suspicion: fate may have an author.

chapters.title: The Concierge's Blind Spot
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Reviewing their own meticulous records, Dominic realizes the one person they never logged is their dearest friend, Marta, the hotel's night manager — whose name fits the ledger's Friday entry. The beat is betrayal and self-doubt; the observer missed themselves.

chapters.title: What Quentin Won't Say
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin admits he was sent here by his dying father to complete the pattern, but came instead hoping someone would stop him. He and Dominic grow close over the decoded pages. The beat is tenderness blooming inside a countdown — love against duty taking shape.

chapters.title: Friday, Early
chapters.summary: Marta's POV (first time). Marta, aware she's being watched, moves the Friday event up a day, locking down the hotel under pretext of a storm. Dominic realizes the trap has closed around all of them. The beat is claustrophobic acceleration.

chapters.title: The Last Entry
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Decoding the ledger's final line, Dominic learns the true design: the pattern requires a witness, and the ledger names them. Marta confronts them with a gun, revealing she has kept the fiction alive for years to protect the hotel. The beat is the climax's first blow.

chapters.title: Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin offers himself in Marta's place, confessing publicly to a murder that never happened to break the cycle. In the chaos, Dominic uses the ledger against Marta, forcing her surrender as police arrive. The beat is sacrifice answered by wit — the climax resolved.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, weeks later. The hotel reopens under new management; Quentin stays, his name entered in the registry as a guest, nothing more. Dominic writes a new first page in the ledger — blank, theirs to fill. The beat is quiet hope: survival's price paid, family found, love chosen over duty.
